title: Opening hours across time zones
description:
A shop in one time zone is open at set hours on some days. Write `record OpeningHours(ZoneId zone, Set<DayOfWeek> days, LocalTime opens, LocalTime closes)` with:

- `boolean isOpen(Instant moment)`: true when, in the shop's zone, the day is one of `days` and the time is at or after `opens` and before `closes`.
- `Instant nextOpening(Instant moment)`: the next moment (at or after `moment`) when the shop opens. If it is open right now, return `moment` itself. Search at most 7 days ahead; `days` empty throws `IllegalStateException`.
- `String describe(Instant moment, ZoneId viewer)`: if open, `"open until HH:mm"`; otherwise `"opens EEE HH:mm"` (for example `"opens Mon 09:00"`), both shown in the **viewer's** zone, with an English locale.

`opens` is always before `closes` (no overnight hours).
hints: Convert the moment into the shop's zone first: `moment.atZone(zone)` gives the local day of the week and the local time to compare with `opens` and `closes`.

For `nextOpening`, walk forward day by day from the local date; on each opening day, `ZonedDateTime.of(date, opens, zone).toInstant()` is the opening moment. Take the first one that is not before `moment`.
`withZoneSameInstant(viewer)` (or `instant.atZone(viewer)`) shows the same moment on the viewer's clock.
